result:
`work run` with no initiative now takes every initiative that is neither done nor abandoned, and the three scenarios r66, r81 and r82 pass. I committed it as cd24b26 on `work/w134`.

**Test runs:**
- `python3 -m pytest -q --work-item w134` gives 147 passed and 1 skipped.
- `tests/scenarios/test_supervision.py` with `--whole-suite` gives 155 passed and 7 xfailed, four runs in a row after the push lock.
- I did not run the whole suite.
- `tools size` prints nothing.
- r66 failed about one run in four before I serialised pushes (see the third item below).

**What it does:**
- The new `scripts/supervise_all.py` gives each open initiative its own run in its own thread, all pulled side by side.
- The runs share one lock, one cap on simultaneous `claude -p` sessions, and one record of what each has written but not yet committed.
- Output has one line per initiative with its status, then its work-items and capability-proposals indented under it.
- The exit code is 1 when a node failed or a run was refused, 3 when a node is awaiting an answer, and 0 otherwise.
- Gate rounds and the move to awaiting-answer come from the already-merged w146 and w152, as the 2026-10-24 answer asks.
- I added the `scripts/supervise_all.py` row to the module map in `CLAUDE.md`.

**Three changes beyond the plan:**
- **`supervise_review.py` outside the file set:** I edited it, which is outside the work-item's file set and named in the report under `## Outside the file set`. The branch review wrote and committed in the checkout without the lock, so another initiative's worker put its files back. Its keep-and-commit now runs under the shared lock.
- **Review session cap:** the review session now takes a place under the shared session cap.
- **`git_push` lock:** `git_push` in `supervise_faults.py` now takes the shared lock, because concurrent pushes of the one branch failed with "cannot lock ref".

**Open questions:**
- An initiative with no work-items, like i2 in r66, still gets a branch review, as a single-initiative run already does.
- With every initiative committing on the one checked-out branch (the 2026-10-24 answer), a later initiative's branch review is skipped when the branch has nothing unread.

**Caveat on the red run:** I recorded a separate red run only for r82 (it failed at the `prints_initiatives` Then). For r81 I wrote the Given and the production code before re-running it alone, so its separate red wasn't recorded; the start-of-work `--work-item w134` run had all five scenarios failing. The report says so.
